title: Star trails over the VLT in Paranal
caption: Star trails over the Auxiliary Telescopes, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Long, bright stripes streak across the dark sky over three of the four Auxiliary Telescopes of the Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI) at ESO's Paranal Observatory. Each stripe is a star trail, the apparent track of a single star as Earth rotates.

Trails like these also bring out the stars' natural colors, and color is a guide to temperature. According to ESO, the reddest stars are about 1000 degrees Celsius, while the hottest, which look blue, reach a few tens of thousands of degrees Celsius. Those colors are on show here in the trails above the domes.

The photographer, ESO Photo Ambassador Babak A. Tafreshi, worked under an extremely clear sky free of light pollution, thanks to the remote, high location in Chile. Those conditions are what make such a vivid display of light possible.

understand.summary: This is a long-exposure star-trail photograph by Babak A. Tafreshi. The source does not publish camera or color-processing details.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as points. The trails come from Earth's rotation during the exposure, and ESO notes the technique also enhances the stars' natural colors.
